hints: Focus on how addition polymerisation works, the C=C double bond opens up to give a two-carbon repeat unit with only single bonds.
Count the atoms over a two-carbon section of the chain, on average you get one Cl for every two carbons and three H for every two carbons.
Work backwards by putting the double bond back between two carbons that together contain that same C2H3Cl composition.
walkthrough:
**Recall addition polymerisation**

Think of the monomer alkene opening its double bond to join up. Each monomer $C=C$ becomes $-C-C-$ in the polymer chain.

$$\text{monomer } C=C \rightarrow \text{polymer } -C-C-$$

**Count atoms in the polymer section**

Look at the 12 carbons shown. There are 6 Cl atoms in total. That is an average of 1 Cl per 2 carbons.

Counting H in the same way gives 3 H per 2 carbons, so the average two-carbon unit is $\text{C}_2\text{H}_3\text{Cl}$.

**Rebuild the monomer**

To get back to the monomer, take a $\text{C}_2$ unit and restore the double bond. A $\text{C}_2\text{H}_3\text{Cl}$ unit must come from $\text{CH}_2=\text{CHCl}$.

$$-\text{CH}_2-\text{CHCl}- \leftarrow \text{CH}_2=\text{CHCl}$$

**Allow for different orientations**

Do not worry that some $\text{Cl}$ atoms are on top and some are underneath, or that $\text{CH}_2$ groups sometimes meet. That is just head-to-tail and head-to-head joining. The atom count still proves the monomer.

options.A: Incorrect. $\text{CHCl}=\text{CHCl}$ would give two Cl atoms per two carbons in the polymer, a $-\text{CHCl}-\text{CHCl}-$ repeat. The diagram has only about one Cl per two carbons, so this has too much chlorine.
options.B: Correct. $\text{CH}_2=\text{CHCl}$ (chloroethene, vinyl chloride) opens to give $-\text{CH}_2-\text{CHCl}-$. Over 12 carbons this gives 6 Cl atoms, exactly as shown. This is poly(chloroethene), PVC.
options.C: Incorrect. $\text{CH}_3\text{CCl}=\text{CHCl}$ has three carbons. An addition polymer from it would contain methyl branches and $\text{C}_3$ repeat units, but the diagram shows a straight chain with only $\text{CH}_2$ and $\text{CHCl}$ groups and no $\text{CH}_3$ or $\text{CCl}$ groups.
options.D: Incorrect. $\text{CH}_3\text{CCl}=\text{CH}_2$ also has three carbons and would give a branched repeat containing $\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)(\text{Cl})$. The polymer shown has no methyl side chains and only two-carbon building blocks.
